metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, November 12, 1876, page 7

facts.fact: Allen skipped out to Windsor, Ontario, to avoid prosecution for violating Kentucky statutes in the Goss-Allen fight
Allen was arrested in Chicago at the instance of Kentucky officers and gave $1,000 bail to appear before Justice Scully, but failed to appear; his bondsman was Mike McDonald
When arrested, Allen protested that he had no intention of avoiding his trial set for November 20

Billy Harrison, advance agent of Mace and Allen, was in Cheyenne on his way to California to prepare exhibitions by the two; some believed Allen meant to reach the Pacific coast out of his Kentucky prosecutors' reach

notes: Text now covers the Tom Allen section; earlier concerns about the cut-off crop are resolved. Mike McDonald also went to Allen's house to levy on his effects and found little.
